correctness.rationale: From the nonzero-product condition, alpha decomposes into fixed-j permutations; theta into fixed-i permutations. Parity of middle coordinates proves n even. The explicit formula is inverted coordinate-by-coordinate for alpha and theta for all even n, including n=2. At n=2, direct local permutation analysis proves exactly 16 admissible first blocks and exactly two second blocks per first, hence 32; an independent 8! exhaustive checker corroborates the finite count.

Its Latin-square count concerns trivial maximal subgroup; the group-bearing nine-element case is outside the exact enumeration. Completed semantic searches returned no covering indexed mathematical finding. The 32-count and explicit all-even formula were separately verified and not implied as formulas by the published existential statement, subject to residual risks.
residual_risks: The 2025 presentation is dated but its exact online upload date is not independently timestamped; the 2026 arXiv release date is verified.
Unindexed earlier semigroup-transversal enumerations may already contain the nine-element count or an equivalent normal form.
The 2026 paper gives broad constructive existence methods; a derived coordinate formula may overlap an implicit special case of those methods even though it is not explicitly stated there.
Relevant primary sections of a long 2026 article were examined, not every page line-by-line.

value.rationale: The nine-element B2(C2) is the smallest Brandt semigroup whose maximal subgroup has no complete mapping but whose full semigroup has one, a natural first counting case at the obstruction boundary. Exact full transversal counts are central to extension of Latin-square enumeration to Rees semigroups, and differ from the established five-element trivial-group count. The uniform all-even construction gives an explicit family-wide witness and isolates the parity mechanism. These are structural and motivated, not arbitrary finite table re-computations.
